sections.html:
Georgetown owners usually weigh three paths: list with an agent, sell privately, or take a cash purchase. Scott County's offices handle the tax bill, the recorded deed and, for owners who fell behind, the delinquent-tax process. Georgetown is the Scott County seat and the sixth-largest city in Kentucky. It was counted at 37,086 in 2020 and is now estimated at 40,883 (July 2025), up 8.9% since the April 2020 base.

Housing here is pricier than in most Kentucky towns. The middle home value among owners is $265,400, median gross rent is $1,255, and 62.3% of households own. Median household income is $80,088. The city has 14,899 households, and growth has kept the market busy, so a clean, priced-right house tends to draw interest.

• Owner-occupancy rate: 62.3%
  • Middle home value among owners: $265,400
  • Median gross rent: $1,255
  • Households: 14,899, with 2.56 persons each
  • Median household income: $80,088

Households with children under 18 made up 38.3% of the total in 2020, and the vacancy rate for rentals was 7.1%. Family buyers drive much of the demand, so a house with bedrooms, a yard and a solid roof shows well.

Georgetown sits in the Bluegrass, north of Lexington. Interstate 75 passes east of downtown with exits 125, 126, 127 and 129, putting downtown Lexington 16 miles south and Cincinnati 69 miles north. U.S. 25 runs through the center, U.S. 62 forms a bypass along the south and east, and U.S. 460 leads 18 miles west to Frankfort.

Toyota Motor Manufacturing Kentucky, which opened in 1988, is the anchor employer, and the population climbed from 18,080 in 2000 to 29,098 in 2010 and 37,086 in 2020. Buyers who work at the plant or commute to Lexington tend to shop close to the interstate exits.

Before a showing, check gutters, roof drainage and basement moisture. Summers run humid and the area sees roughly 45 inches of precipitation a year, so inspectors look at those items first.

sections.h2: How Scott County collects property tax
sections.html:
The Scott County Sheriff collects tax for 28 districts, and bills are normally mailed on November 1. The sheriff does not set values. Questions about an assessment go to the Scott County PVA, on the second floor of the courthouse at 101 East Main Street, or by phone at (502) 863-7885.

Payment can be cash, cashier's check, money order or card. Cards add a 2.75% vendor fee. The bill itself shows the due dates, how to avoid penalties and what to do if a mortgage company pays for you.

If you are behind on taxes, the clerk's schedule below shows how little time passes before costs pile up.

Delinquent tax timeline in Scott County
WhenWhat happens
April 15Delinquent certificates move to the County Clerk's office
May and JuneThe County Attorney mails two notices, and the first offers a payment agreement to eligible owners
June 30Last day to enter a payment agreement
July 1Advertising costs are added to bills still unpaid, which are published in the newspaper
Late summerPayment is due by a cutoff before the annual delinquent tax sale

When a bill transfers, a 10% penalty and the sheriff's add-on fee are already attached, and interest runs at 1% per month. Ask the clerk for a payoff figure before you pick a closing date. That amount comes out of your sale proceeds, so you want it firm before you accept any offer.

On a sale, the seller covers a state deed tax of $0.50 per $500 of value, with any partial block counted as a full one. You pay it at the Scott County Clerk's counter, 101 East Main Street, when the deed goes on record. The office keeps weekday hours from 8:30 to 4:30 and answers at (502) 863-7875.

Owners past 65 or with a total disability may qualify for the state homestead exemption, $49,100 in the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, through the Scott County PVA. The benefit follows the owner, so whoever buys your house must apply on their own.

The City of Georgetown handles building permits for both the city and Scott County, from the Building Inspection Department at 125 West Clinton Street. Zoning, plats and floodplain information come from the Georgetown-Scott County Planning Commission, which offers a zoning map and a plat finder on its site and answers at (502) 867-3701.

For a house with an addition or a finished basement, ask the building department whether the permits were closed. A buyer's title review goes faster when the paperwork matches the house. If the house has been rented by the night, ask the planning office whether a registration applies.

Once you accept an offer, a closing agent or attorney orders a title search. That search turns up the mortgage, any unpaid tax certificate and any recorded lien, and each one must be paid or released from your proceeds. Ask the sheriff and the clerk for written payoff figures a few days before the closing date so the settlement statement matches the real bills.

On closing day you sign the deed, the seller pays the transfer tax to the clerk, and the deed is recorded in Scott County. Property tax for the part of the year you owned the house is usually prorated on the statement. A cash buyer can often close on a date you choose, since there is no appraisal or loan underwriting to wait for. A conventional buyer needs time for the lender, and a failed appraisal can reopen price talks.

If you plan to move out first, leave the utilities on until the deed is recorded, hand over keys and garage openers at the table, and keep copies of the signed paperwork.

sections.h2: Choosing a route for your house
sections.html:
Before you compare offers, gather these items:

  • The current and prior year tax bills from the sheriff, plus any delinquent certificate from the clerk.
  • A mortgage payoff statement, and the release for any other recorded lien.
  • Permit records from the City of Georgetown for additions or major repairs.
  • Leases and tenant contacts for any rented unit.

A house in good order with time to market suits an agent. A private sale needs an attorney for the contract and deed. Deferred repairs, tenants, delinquent taxes or an estate point toward a cash offer, which skips showings, appraisal and lender approval. Whatever the route, judge offers by what remains after payoff, deed tax, prorated property tax and repair credits.

faqs.q: How much deed tax applies to a Georgetown sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays $0.50 for every $500 of value, rounded up, at the Scott County Clerk's counter when the deed is filed.

faqs.q: When does Scott County mail property tax bills?
faqs.a: The Scott County Sheriff normally mails them on November 1. The bill lists the due dates, how to avoid penalties and what to do if a mortgage company pays.

faqs.q: What happens to unpaid Georgetown property taxes?
faqs.a: Around April 15 they move to the Scott County Clerk. The County Attorney mails notices in May and June, advertising costs attach on July 1, and a bill still open can go to the annual delinquent tax sale.

faqs.q: Which office answers questions on a Georgetown assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Scott County Property Valuation Administrator at (502) 863-7885. The sheriff collects the bill but does not set the value.

faqs.q: Where do I get a building permit in Georgetown?
faqs.a: The City of Georgetown's Building Inspection Department, 125 West Clinton Street, issues permits for both Georgetown and Scott County. Zoning and plat questions go to the Georgetown-Scott County Planning Commission, (502) 867-3701.
